To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a simple yet effective method of creating a perturbable donor-acceptor system with multicolor fluorescence responses toward nonmetalloprotesins and metalloprotein, which holds great potential for visual protein sensing.

we have successfully created a perturbable multicolor fluorescence sensing platform for proteins, which is composed of a blend of conjugated polyelelctrolytes (PPEs) and a fluorescent dye, and the sensing platform can be applied to detect both nonmetalloprotein and metalloprotein.

blending two conjugated polyelelctrolytes with different emission wavelengths can be a convenient yet powerful strategy to create a perturable energy donor-accepter assembly with multicolor response toward both non-metalloproteins, e.g., BSA and HSA, and metalloprotons, e.g., Zn(II) and Cu(II), which holds great promise for visual sensing and imaging of proteins.

the blending of conjugated polyelelectrolytes (CPEs) is an effective way to construct multicolor fluorescent protein sensing system, in which the energy transfer from the donor to the acceptor can be modulated by proteins.

The main takeaway from our work is that
blending conjugated polymers with different emission wavelengths can create a multicolor perturbable energy-transfer system with a wide variety of applications.
conjugated polyelec-trolytes (CPs) can be blended with each other to form a perturbable donor-acceptor system, which can be used to create multicolor fluorescence response.
